text:
deploy-bot: rolling deploy started for service=frontend-service namespace=prod from image=frontend:v42 -> frontend:v43 (canary=10%)
Maya Rivera: paging: saw ~25% 500s for frontend-service in eu-west-1, alert fire. seeing CrashLoopBackOff on canary pods.
deploy-bot: canary pods (frontend-v43-*) started 2023-11-11T09:10:56Z -> readiness failing on 2/3 replicas
Maya Rivera: logs on one canary: `panic: nil pointer` during cache init. stack points at new cache adapter code.
Alex Chen: confirming, `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=frontend,version=v43` -> 3 pods, 2 CrashLoopBackOff, 1 Ready but high latency.
Jon Peters: I'm on call. @Maya can you paste the liveness/readiness probe config from the canary manifest?
Maya Rivera: here's the probe snippet from the manifest we rolled (note: new helm chart change):
```yaml
livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 10
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /ready
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 3
  periodSeconds: 5
```
Maya Rivera: initialDelaySeconds was lowered in the chart override to speed up readiness. suspect the service needs longer init for the new cache.
Jon Peters: ok that + new adapter panic explains the CrashLoop. Also noticed HPA in prod pointing at cpuUtilization target=20 and minReplicas=1 for frontend; with canary misbehaving HPA scaled down older replicas?
Alex Chen: HPA config for frontend in prod: `minReplicas: 1` `maxReplicas: 40` `targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 20`. Canary being unhealthy caused service -> some nodes evicted -> traffic got routed disproportionately -> 500s for subset of customers.
SRE Rotation Bot: incident-7421 created: PROD_CANARY_CRASH_FRONTEND -> severity=sev2. Pages to oncall.
Jon Peters: immediate mitigation steps: 1) pause rollout/cancel canary 2) enable kill-switch feature flag for new cache 3) rollback frontend to v42 if needed 4) revert liveness/readiness quick-change to safe defaults 5) scale up stable replica set to absorb traffic.
Priya Singh: I'm toggling feature flag `enable_new_cache` to false for prod canary via LaunchDarkly. Doing it now.
Priya Singh: toggled -> @everyone: kill-switch ON for account segment=all, rule=all users :white_check_mark:
Maya Rivera: after kill-switch, panic gone from logs of the remaining canary. but pods still CrashLoopBackOff due to rapid restarts and low initialDelay.
Jon Peters: scale stable RS: `kubectl scale deploy frontend --replicas=20 -n prod` to absorb traffic. Doing now.
Alex Chen: scaled stable to 20, traffic drop of 500s to ~5% within 2 minutes. good.
Jon Peters: pause rollout: `kubectl rollout pause deploy/frontend -n prod` and mark canary as failed in deployment tool.
Jon Peters: also undo the rollout for safety: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/frontend -n prod --to-revision=REVISION_V42` (we have revision tag). preparing to run.
Maya Rivera: before undo, can we try quick patch to livenessProbe to avoid immediate restarts? patching to `initialDelaySeconds: 30` for canary pods so they stabilize and we can collect more logs. Command: `kubectl patch deploy frontend -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"frontend","livenessProbe":{"initialDelaySeconds":30}}]}}}}' -n prod`
Jon Peters: good call. Do that on canary label only: `kubectl patch deploy/frontend -p ... --selector=version=v43 -n prod` (note: kubectl patch on deploy doesn't accept selector; need to patch replicaset/pod template) — let's keep it simple: we're undoing rollout to be safe.
Nikhil Rao: CS bot reporting: Customer Success saw ~120 customers had errors between 09:10-09:18 in EU cluster, mostly read-only endpoints. I've posted a banner draft to send: "We're investigating elevated errors on certain endpoints; root cause under investigation. No payment or data loss."
Customer Success Bot: Notified customers on status.redwood.ai and opened a support incident for top 5 customers.
Jon Peters: rollback done: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/frontend -n prod` -> rollout status shows stable v42 back to 20 replicas and ready.
deploy-bot: rollout undo finished, canary marks removed, traffic rebalanced.
Maya Rivera: after rollback, error rate back to baseline in eu-west within 5 minutes. Great.
Jon Peters: follow-up actions while incident still open: - create PR to revert the liveness/readiness chart override - add Canary guard: block chart config changes that reduce initialDelay below 15s for frontend - add integration test to exercise cache adapter init path - update HPA to `minReplicas: 3` for prod frontend during business hours to avoid single-point scale-down.
Alex Chen: I'll open the PR for chart revert and add the guard in CI, tagging @Maya and @Priya.
Maya Rivera: logging note: captured stack traces and added to internal bug tracker RB-1183.
Jon Peters: postmortem items: customer impact: ~120 customers affected, 8 customers opened support tickets, no data loss. Timeline: deploy started 09:10, alerts 09:12, kill-switch toggled 09:14, rollback started 09:16, rollback complete 09:21, resolved 09:22.
SRE Rotation Bot: handoff scheduled: @Jon Peters handing to @Nikhil Rao at 10:00 UTC.
Nikhil Rao: ack, will take next watch and continue cleanup.
Priya Singh: will coordinate CS follow-ups and update status page with resolved + root cause note.
Jon Peters: root cause (preliminary): twofold - 1) unsafe chart override lowered probe initialDelay causing restarts during cache init, 2) new cache adapter had an init-time race that caused panics on first start. HPA + minReplicas=1 amplified impact.
Maya Rivera: mitigations applied: kill-switch, rollback, temporary scale-up, incident opened.
Jon Peters: marking incident-7421 as mitigated, will convert to postmortem and assign action owners.
Customer Success Bot: status page updated to RESOLVED. Customers notified.
Maya Rivera: thanks everyone. I'll file the postmortem draft and include logs/commands.
Jon Peters: great job fast responses. After-action owners: Alex - chart revert PR, Maya - root-cause bug, Priya - customer comms, Nikhil - HPA tunings and canary policy.
Maya Rivera: closing thread after postmortem created.
SRE Rotation Bot: incident-7421 status -> mitigated -> severity downgraded to sev3 for postmortem.
